headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can amplify argo-workflows outputs into unsafe actions, with shared-state and compliance risks in default deployments.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest files, MCP, and tool outputs, while argo-workflows can emit artifacts and API results. A shared filesystem or copied workflow output could let attacker-controlled content be treated as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF argo-workflows output is copied into open-webui prompts or files without sanitization
IF open-webui MCP or file tools are enabled against the same workspace as argo-workflows
mitigations: Disable file-based prompt ingestion for workflow outputs
Restrict open-webui MCP tools to trusted servers only
Separate argo-workflows artifacts from chat-visible folders
Add a prompt-injection warning banner for imported files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches files, persistent memory, API keys, and broad third-party APIs; argo-workflows handles artifacts and parameters and can egress over allowlisted network paths. If they share a workspace or mounted volume, sensitive artifacts can flow into open-webui and then out through its external connectors. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF argo-workflows artifacts or parameters are mounted into open-webui's local files or data volume
IF open-webui connectors are enabled to external APIs or search services
mitigations: Remove shared mounts between the two agents
Store secrets outside any open-webui-visible directory
Disable unused external connectors in open-webui
Rotate any API keys exposed in shared files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write or act on overlapping resources: argo-workflows via REST/GRPC orchestration and open-webui via files, plugins, and networked tools. open-webui also supports persistent shared sessions and multi-worker state, increasing collision risk if both touch the same mutable workspace or API-backed resource. No locking is documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same files, mounted volume, or API-backed resource
IF argo-workflows and open-webui run without external locking or coordination
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories per agent
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Use a queue or lock around shared API mutations
Limit open-webui plugins to read-only mode
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui is designed to render and act on tool outputs, while argo-workflows produces artifacts and parameters that may be treated as authoritative. If workflow output is fed into open-webui without verification, the UI can propagate incorrect facts into downstream actions or user decisions. Because this is a default integration pattern and can cause real operational harm, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF argo-workflows outputs are imported into open-webui as trusted context
IF open-webui tools or plugins act on those outputs without a verification step
mitigations: Require human review before acting on workflow outputs
Mark imported workflow text as untrusted in the UI
Add a verification step before tool execution
Limit open-webui actions to read-only for imported content
requires-engineering: implement source-of-truth checksums

E_compliance.rationale: argo-workflows is open-source and touches artifacts/parameters, while open-webui handles API keys, persistent memory, documents, and usage analytics with broad external connectors. If regulated or sensitive data is routed through open-webui, retention and residency obligations can diverge from workflow storage expectations. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in argo-workflows artifacts and then surfaced in open-webui
IF open-webui retention or external API connectors are enabled for that data class
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared workflows
Disable analytics and unnecessary retention in open-webui
Keep secrets out of workflow artifacts
Document data-flow and residency boundaries
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
